note_two_verbs: THIS FAMILY HAS TWO RIVAL CREATE VERBS AND THEY MODEL DIFFERENT THINGS. `plumbing.create` = a PIPE (kind/origin/diameter/bendRadius), writes the plugin DTO store, has a CEB case, and NOTHING subscribes to its event. `plumbing.createFixture` = a FIXTURE (toilet/sink/bath/shower), has NO CEB case and NO initTools bridge, and is the route that actually renders — it bridges straight to the legacy CreatePlumbingFixtureCommand. The census's 'CEB case but no initTools bridge, yet reachable by another route' is exactly this: the OTHER ROUTE IS `plumbing.createFixture`.

SILENT-SUCCESS-ON-FAILURE: CreatePlumbingFixture.ts wraps the execute in `try { … } catch (e) { console.error(…) }` and then returns `{ forward: [], inverse: [] }` — a SUCCESS. In a browser where `window.commandManager` is absent or the command throws, the bus reports success and nothing is created. Its sibling CreateRoomHandler in the same repo THROWS by name in exactly that situation (measured: B4 P-I). This is the ADR-0299 §RECOVERY-MUST-REFUSE shape.

findings.claim: packages/command-bus/src/commands.ts:792 declares `'plumbing.create': { fixtureType: string; position: {x,y,z}; levelId?: string }`. CreatePlumbingHandler reads `kind`/`origin`/`diameter`/`bendRadius`. A dispatcher that OBEYS the declared type gets a silently defaulted 50 mm cold-water straight pipe at world origin — the exact defect §FIX-PLUMBING-FIXTURE-CMD fixed at ONE call site while leaving the type declaration that invites it in place. This is the same shape as B4-FURN-01 (commands.ts:781 for furniture).

packages/geometry-plumbing/src/PlumbingTool.ts:414 and :455 fire `bus.executeCommand('plumbing.create', {})` as 'bus telemetry' beside the real `commandManager.execute(CreatePlumbingFixtureCommand)`. The handler accepts `{}`, mints an id, commits a levelId-less pipe and takes an undo slot. Every 3-D fixture placement therefore leaves a phantom pipe in the DTO store and pushes two undo entries.

findings.class: SILENT SUCCESS ON FAILURE (the refusing half has no escape hatch)
findings.claim: CreatePlumbingFixtureHandler.execute() catches every error from the legacy command, console.errors it, and returns `{ forward: [], inverse: [] }` — which the bus reads as SUCCESS. If `window.commandManager` is absent it does not even try: `if (cm) { … }` and then the same empty success. The plan tool's `.catch()` therefore never fires and the user is told a toilet exists that was never created. CreateRoomHandler, in the same repo and the same shape, THROWS by name instead — so the correct pattern is already written down here.
findings.contract_clause: C16 §5.1 CA-21 / ADR-0299 §RECOVERY-MUST-REFUSE — 'a bridge that cannot reach authoritative state THROWS. It never returns an empty patch pair, because an empty patch pair is indistinguishable from applied, nothing to change.' (quoted from plugins/rooms/src/handlers/CreateRoom.ts, the sibling that got it right)

findings.claim: The reachable fixture route registers the element with bimManager (CreatePlumbingFixtureCommand.ts:64) but never with viewDependencyTracker, unlike the §FT-FURNITURE / §FT-WALL bridges which call both (§FIX-PLAN-VDT-BIMMANAGER). Every plumbing store event therefore misses the O(1) `_elementLevelMap` lookup and falls to ViewDependencyTracker's `_resolveElementLevelId` fallback — the §G3-STALE path the curtain-panel work (OI-054) identified as an O(views) sweep plus a console.warn per element.

C11 §11's per-element compliance matrix has no Plumbing row at all, even though §11.11 documents a shipped fix for the family and C11 §11 says the matrix 'MUST be updated whenever a bridge is added, removed, or repaired'. A family with no row cannot be read as compliant or non-compliant; it is invisible to the artefact an engineer consults before touching it. The concrete cost: nothing in §11 records that `plumbing.create` survived the fix as a live, ghost-producing, orphan-channelled verb.
